identity.name: PURAVANKARA LIMITED
identity.industry: Residential Real Estate / Premium Urban Development & Commercial Asset Monetization

summary.oneLiner: Puravankara delivered record presales of INR7,407cr in FY26 (55% YoY growth) and EBITDA margin expansion to 22% in Q4, driven by premium launches and redevelopment wins; the company now targets INR11,200cr presales in FY27 with INR750cr net debt reduction, signaling a structural shift from volume to value-driven growth with strong balance sheet discipline.

one-line thesis: Puravankara delivered record presales of INR7,407cr in FY26 (55% YoY growth) and EBITDA margin expansion to 22% in Q4, driven by premium launches and redevelopment wins; the company now targets INR11,200cr presales in FY27 with INR750cr net debt reduction, signaling a structural shift from volume to value-driven growth with strong balance sheet discipline.
financial scorecard: revenue: INR3,846cr (+84% YoY); EBITDA/margin: INR339cr (+190% YoY) at 22% (Q4); PAT (rptd): INR111cr (Q4) vs loss of INR88cr (Q4FY25); PAT (normalized): N/A (no major one-offs); order book: INR11,200cr FY27 presales target (not traditional order book); net debt: INR2,321cr as of Mar'26 (-INR160cr QoQ), net debt/equity 1.31x
guidance: revenue growth: INR11,200cr presales target for FY27 (+51% YoY); margin: sustained 20%+ EBITDA margins expected across premium launches; order inflow: 48% from existing portfolio, 52% from new launches; capex/commissioning: INR750cr debt reduction target (excl. strategic BD), no explicit capex guidance but land acquisition and project development funded via incremental debt and cash flow
order book & pipeline: INR11,200cr presales target for FY27 (not traditional order book); current land bank: 56.48M sq.ft; launch pipeline GDV: INR22,547cr across 14.85M sq.ft
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: 7.25M sq.ft sold in FY26, avg realization INR10,213/sq.ft; Commercial: Zentech (44% leased/sold), Aerocity (leasing underway), Thane retail (3L sq.ft); Redevelopment: Chembur (1.2M sq.ft, GDV INR2,100cr), Malabar Hills (0.7M sq.ft, GDV INR2,700cr); Plotted: margins 35-40%; New launches: Purva Northern Lights (INR1,100-1,200cr Q4 presales, INR10,700/sq.ft), Purva Estrella (INR800cr+ presales, >20% margin)
growth verticals / optionality: Entry into data centers (leasing-only model), warehousing, retail expansion; NCR (Delhi-Noida-Gurgaon) as next geographic expansion; Starworth (unlisted) has INR2,000cr+ order book
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin 22% (up from 12% in FY25); premium projects yield 20-21% gross margins; redevelopment projects target 20%+; plotted projects 35-40%; construction costs up 6-7% due to diesel, but mitigated by pricing power and contingencies
capex / expansion: No explicit capex guidance; incremental debt used for business development (INR15,200cr GDV added in FY26); land acquisition and project development funded via debt and operating cash flow; no greenfield capex beyond existing pipeline
capital allocation: Priority: INR750cr net debt reduction in FY27; then strategic business development (land acquisition, JDA); no dividend guidance; cash balance of INR1,695cr as of Mar'26 supports flexibility
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical uncertainty impacting NRI demand; regulatory delays in approvals (esp. Bengaluru); construction cost inflation; execution risk in large redevelopment projects (Malabar Hills, Chembur); commercial leasing velocity may lag projections
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; strong emphasis on balance sheet health, premiumization, and execution capability; transparent on challenges (approval delays) but optimistic on demand resilience; no overpromising on timelines
non-obvious takeaways: INR600cr+ interest expense includes fair-value accounting for equity-linked debt (NCDs), not just cash interest; Starworth’s INR2,000cr+ order book is unconsolidated but material; Malabar Hills pricing at INR115k-120k/sq.ft implies ultra-premium positioning; 35M sq.ft land bank remains after FY27 pipeline execution

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
